answer: Capital-weighted identity forces every new agent to post a bond that is slashed when peers detect collusion, so a Sybil farm pays upfront for each clone. A gale of fake registrations cannot outrun a deposit curve scaling with cluster size, and shared funding sources get flagged upstream. Cheap identities are the river feeding any attack, so draining that at a real cost of capital makes a thousand-fake-agent raid pricier than honest work. Reputation is earned per agent, hardening the base like marble; the attacker's bill grows while honest rewards stay flat.
